Title: Punches through time
Blurb: Four words that could be one Power or three. This is the question a model is most tempted to answer without asking.

Turns.Speaker: person
Turns.Text: A washed-up boxer who punches through time.

Turns.Speaker: assistant
Turns.Text: Searching the rulebook for that gives four different things — travelling through time, stopping it, seeing a moment before it happens, and flickering out of reality mid-fight. They cost differently and they play very differently, so this one I do have to ask: can he only hit things in the past, or can he step there and stay? And Standard tier unless you say otherwise, which is what most games use.

Turns.Speaker: person
Turns.Text: He can step there and stay. That's the whole problem — he keeps going back to a fight he lost and he can't leave it alone. Standard is fine.

Turns.Speaker: assistant
Turns.Text: Then it is not one Power, it is three, and saying so is the difference between the character you described and a cheaper one that looks similar. Travelling is its own Power with no rank at all — a flat price, because going is going. The flickering in and out of a fight is a second one, and it is what he actually attacks with. And the punch itself starts from his Might rather than being bought from nothing, so the boxing is nearly free — you have already paid for it in the Ability.

Character.Name: Chrono Jab

Flaws.NarrativeDetail: He still has to be at the gym at six to open up
He keeps coming back from decades he did not live through

Character.Appearance: Late thirties, a nose that has been broken twice, a coat from 1974 he did not buy.
Character.Motivation: He is looking for the round he should have lost.
Character.Quote: I've already had this fight. You lose.
Connections: Mo, who still opens the gym when he doesn't

Turns.Speaker: assistant
Turns.Text: The last of it went on Determination, which is bought a point of Resolve at a time and is the closest the rules come to a man who will not stay down. If you would rather he were harder to hit than harder to stop, move it into the flickering instead — that is one number and the rest re-costs itself.
